sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns, true/false or a short passage).

questions.q: Read the passage and answer: 'Banana plants grown by farmers are genetically similar to the parent plant. Such plants are produced without the fusion of gametes.' (a) Name the method used to grow genetically similar banana plants. (b) Name two types of asexual reproduction.
questions.answer: (a) Vegetative propagation. (b) Any two: binary fission, budding, spore formation, vegetative propagation.

questions.q: Read the passage on RTIs and STDs and answer: (a) Which of these is NOT a sexually transmitted disease — syphilis, gonorrhoea, goitre, herpes? (b) HIV is NOT transmitted by — sharing infected needles / casual contact such as hugging / infected blood / unprotected sex?
questions.answer: (a) Goitre. (b) Casual contact such as hugging (or sharing food, toilets, mosquito bites).

questions.q: Read the passage on pollination and answer: (a) What is self-pollination? (b) What is cross-pollination?
questions.answer: (a) Transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower (or another flower of the same plant). (b) Transfer of pollen from the anther of a flower to the stigma of a flower on another plant of the same species.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Fertilised ovules develop into ________, and the ________ develops into the fruit.
Match: (1) Vas deferens (2) Fallopian tube — (a) produces sperms (b) carries sperms towards the ejaculatory duct (c) site of fertilisation (d) the womb
Write True (T) or False (F): (1) Earthworm is a hermaphrodite. (2) HIV spreads through mosquito bites.

sections.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Growing rose plants from pieces of stem is called —
Joining a shoot of one plant to the rooted stem of another, as in mango, is —
Raising plants from a mass of cells in a nutrient medium is called —
The undifferentiated mass of cells in the bottles is the —
These plants are exact copies of their parents because —
options: they are formed by fusion of gametes
they are formed by asexual (vegetative) methods without fusion of gametes

sections.passage: Kiran visited a plant nursery and saw the gardener growing rose plants from pieces of stem pushed into the soil, mango plants by joining a shoot of one plant to the stem of another, and many tiny plants growing in glass bottles from a mass of cells in a jelly-like nutrient medium. The gardener said that all these plants are exact copies of their parents.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Draw a diagram of a flower and label the stigma and the stamen.
questions.answer: Diagram: a flower in section showing petals and sepals on the thalamus; in the centre the pistil (stigma at the top, style, ovary with ovules at the base); around it the stamens (anther on a filament). Labels: stigma, stamen.

questions.q: In a diagram of a flower the parts A, B and C are the anther, style and ovary. State the function of the ovary.
questions.answer: The ovary contains the ovules (female gametes); after fertilisation the ovules develop into seeds and the ovary into the fruit.

questions.q: Name the type of cell division in: (a) growth of seedlings (b) sperm formation (c) wound healing (d) asexual reproduction in Amoeba.
Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction.
questions.answer: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent and no gametes; the offspring are identical to the parent. Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of male and female gametes; the offspring show variation.

questions.q: Name four methods of contraception.
questions.answer: Condom, Copper-T (IUCD), oral contraceptive pills, vasectomy/tubectomy.

questions.q: Expand HIV and AIDS.
questions.answer: HIV — Human Immunodeficiency Virus; AIDS — Acquired Immuno-Deficiency Syndrome.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Define oviparous, viviparous and hermaphrodite animals with an example of each.
questions.answer: Oviparous animals lay eggs and the young develop outside the mother's body (hen, frog). Viviparous animals give birth to young that develop inside the mother's womb (human, cow). Hermaphrodites have both male and female sex organs in the same individual (earthworm, tapeworm).

or.answer: Adolescence is the stage of life (about 10–19 years) when physical, physiological and psychological changes take place as a child grows into an adult. Puberty is the period when the body undergoes changes that make it capable of reproduction. Menarche is the first menstrual bleeding in a girl.

questions.q: Describe budding in Hydra with a diagram.
questions.answer: In Hydra a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the side of the body due to repeated cell division. It grows, develops a mouth and tentacles, and finally detaches from the parent to live as a new Hydra. Diagram: parent Hydra with a bud at different stages of growth, then a separated young Hydra.

or.q: Name three plants that grow from the stem, and the kind of stem.
or.answer: Potato (tuber), ginger (rhizome), onion (bulb); also lawn grass (runner).

questions.q: Describe binary fission in Amoeba and budding in Hydra with diagrams.
questions.answer: Binary fission: the nucleus of Amoeba divides into two, then the cytoplasm divides, forming two daughter Amoebae; the parent loses its identity. Budding: a bud grows on the body of Hydra, develops tentacles and separates as a new individual. Diagrams show the stages of each.

questions.q: Draw a T.S. of a bisexual flower and label the ovary, ovules, anther and stigma.
questions.answer: Diagram: longitudinal section of a flower with sepals and petals on the thalamus, stamens (anther on filament) around a central pistil whose swollen base, the ovary, contains ovules, with the style and stigma above. Labels: ovary, ovules, anther, stigma.
questions.note: April 2023 also asked for the functions of the stamen (produces pollen), anther (bears pollen), pistil (female part) and ovary (contains ovules that become seeds).

questions.q: What is micropropagation (tissue culture)? State two of its advantages.
questions.answer:
Micropropagation is growing many plants from a small piece of plant tissue in a nutrient medium. Every plant cell is totipotent: the tissue forms an undifferentiated mass, the callus, which with hormones grows into plantlets.
Advantages: a large number of identical plants is obtained quickly from a small piece of tissue; disease-free plants can be raised in any season, including plants that do not produce viable seeds.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the types of asexual reproduction in lower organisms with diagrams and an example each.
questions.answer: (1) Binary fission: in Amoeba and bacteria the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm, giving two daughter cells; the parent loses its identity. (2) Budding: in yeast a bud forms from the mother cell and the elongated nucleus divides, one part entering the bud; in Hydra a bud develops all body parts and detaches. (3) Spore formation: in Chlamydomonas the nucleus and cytoplasm divide to form 4–8 spores, each of which grows into a new individual on release; spores also form in fungi, mosses and ferns. Diagrams show each process.

questions.q: Name the human male and female reproductive organs and state the function of each.
questions.answer: Male: testes — produce sperms and testosterone; vasa deferentia — carry sperms from the testes to the ejaculatory duct; ejaculatory duct — common passage of urine and sperms; penis — transfers sperms into the female body. Female: ovaries — produce ova and oestrogen and progesterone; fallopian tubes — carry ova to the uterus and are the site of fertilisation; uterus — the womb in which the embryo develops; cervix — the opening of the uterus; vagina — the passage to the outside.

questions.q: Describe pollination and fertilisation in flowering plants with a diagram.
questions.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma by wind, water or insects; it may be self-pollination (same flower) or cross-pollination (another plant of the same species). On the stigma the pollen grain grows a pollen tube which passes down the style into the ovary and reaches the ovule; the male nucleus fuses with the egg nucleus (fertilisation). The fertilised ovule becomes the seed and the ovary the fruit; the seed later germinates into a new plant. Diagram: pistil with a pollen grain on the stigma and a pollen tube growing down the style to the ovule.

questions.q: How are STDs and HIV/AIDS transmitted, and how can they be prevented?
questions.answer: STDs (gonorrhoea, syphilis, herpes, chlamydia) spread by sexual contact; symptoms include itching, sores, discharge and painful urination; untreated they can cause infertility. HIV spreads by unprotected sex, transfusion of infected blood, shared needles and from an infected mother to her baby; it destroys T-helper cells, leading to AIDS. It does not spread by touching, hugging, sharing food or toilets, or mosquitoes. Prevention: one faithful partner, correct and consistent use of condoms, sterilised needles and screened blood, early treatment of STDs, and medical advice for infected pregnant women.
